TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_APPLEGREEN_HANDBOOK_S: The Siren's song made everyone lose their way—but not this green apple. It never spoke of the incident until the zombies invaded. Then it began to imitate the Siren's song...
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_APPLE_HANDBOOK_STORY: They say an apple with one bite missing once made its owner rich. Apple Clock found work in another field: zombies startled by its ringing suffer instant cardiopulmonary “arrest.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_BLOVER_HANDBOOK_STORY: On Blover's fifth birthday, he received a sparkling birthday cake. He made a wish, took a deep breath, and blew out only 60 percent of the candles. He refused to give up. That childhood failure drove him to keep training until the present day.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_BOWLINGEGG_HANDBOOK_S:
Unlike other bowling nuts, Bowling Easter Egg has never truly stopped moving. It has been spinning since the instant it touched the ground—and considers that quite an achievement.
“My ribbon wrapping? That's my entrance costume.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_BUNGISQUASH_HANDBOOK_: Bungee Squash was tired of hearing the Squash family mocked for being easy to bait. To avoid falling for the same tricks, he secretly studied Bungee Zombie's landing technique. Now he controls his landing point more precisely than any Squash... Of course, since he still cannot change course after takeoff, he remains just as easy to bait.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_BUTTERGLOOMSHROOM_HAN: Butter Gloom-shroom's butter began as an accident—he fell into a barrel of it. Then he discovered that everyone suddenly liked him, and he became rather less gloomy. “Would you like some butter?” he now asks every customer.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_BYWZ_HANDBOOK_STORY:
Dave usually recycles unwanted seed packets by hiding them in barrels, but lately someone seems to be stealing them. “Come on, rummaging through trash cans is fun! I only looked because it was sparkling...”
Let us hope it does not happen again.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CABBAGECOBX_HANDBOOK_: Promotion brought Taco Cannoneer better equipment: a new helmet, targeting goggles, and a much heavier cannon. For some reason, he feels he should coordinate with other gunners, but he has yet to find the right teammates.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CABBAGECOB_HANDBOOK_S: Despite his decorations and his status as the pride of the cabbage family, Taco Mortar seems unhappy in retirement. “The boss taught me to fight and celebrated my birthdays...” Remembering an old friend, Taco Mortar sighs. “How could such a fine cob just... move into a retirement home? What's wrong with life in the country?”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CABBAGEPULTINSIDE_HAN: Compete-pult cannot read, but that does not stop him from wearing glasses. When asked why he forces himself to study, he smiles and replies, “Peer pressure.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CABBAGEPULT_HANDBOOK_: Cabbage-pult is very good at pelting zombies with cabbages. He makes a living from it; after all, it is what he does best. He still cannot work out how the zombies get onto the roof.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CACTUSBLOVER_HANDBOOK: Cactus Blover likes to end fights quickly. Blowing out that many spikes tires his muscles, yet he never gets tired of doing it. He merely has to endure Three-Cactus muttering in the background.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CACTUS_HANDBOOK_STORY: Cactus may be prickly, but beneath those spines is a gentle heart full of love and kindness. She longs to hug and be hugged, though most people cannot manage it. Cactus does not mind. She studies an armored mouse for a long moment—perhaps this one really is huggable.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CALTROPSNOW_HANDBOOK_: Spikeweed once read a line somewhere: “I've spent my life walking on thin ice. Do you think I'll reach the other shore?” It loved the words so much that it traveled all the way to Antarctica. At last, the zombies would learn what walking on thin ice really felt like.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CALTROPZ_HANDBOOK_STO: Zombie Spikeweed dreams of becoming a scout, but being so short limits the view. Inspired by burrs, he began fastening spiked balls to everyone headed back the other way, sending a small part of himself into the wider world. Naturally, he has never collected any of them.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CARDLESS_HANDBOOK_STO:
Plants disagree about how Holographic Card Projector lowers seed-packet prices. The principle is actually simple: project several copies, absorb a little sun for power, and turn the projections into real seeds—all for less than the original price!
“Future technology, kid!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CATFLOWER_HANDBOOK_ST:
“Peashooter gave me this cat outfit,” says Sunflower. “He thought it looked nice on me.” The side effect is that she occasionally barks, and her concerts have become a mess.
“That's supposed to be our sound!” protests one fan.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CATGATLINGPEA_HANDBOO:
That new outfit on Cosmic Gatling Cattail? It is a co-branded costume from Cattail and Starfruit, and preorders even came with bonus cat stickers!
Most Gatling Peas are too embarrassed to put them on, though...
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CATPOT_HANDBOOK_STORY: “You may not know this,” says Cattail, “but my tail is the real me.” She removes her hat; it is empty inside. Dave promptly fills it with soil. “Call me Litterbox if you must, but anyone who calls me a kitty toilet is asking for trouble!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CATPUMPKIN_HANDBOOK_S:
“Cattail is remarkably adaptable. With just a little adjustment... behold, a perfect new species.”
“One more thing: please do not put zombie cats in the cat bed.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CATTAILZ_HANDBOOK_STO: Zombie Cattail idolizes Black Cat Detective, which is why she fights the other plants for the remote during prime-time cartoons. Incidentally, it took her ages to explain to Cat Bed that she is a plant, not a “zombie cat.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CATTAIL_HANDBOOK_STOR: “Woof!” says Cattail. “Woof, woof! Confused? You didn't assume I'd meow just because my name says cat and I look like one, did you? That's not how things work around here. I refuse to be pigeonholed.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHERRYBEAN_HANDBOOK_S: Coffee Bean is putting the finishing touches on his role in a new stage production, The Little Boy Who Sold Cherries. He takes the part so seriously that he often forgets to remove the cherry costume.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHERRYBOMB_HANDBOOK_S: “I'm about to burst,” says Cherry One. “No, we're about to blow up!” corrects his brother, Cherry Two. Only after a heated discussion do they settle on the word “explode.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHERRYMINE_HANDBOOK_S: Cherry Potato Mine runs a snack stand. “I hear he's moving into instant food and plans to mass-market his signature dish,” says one customer. “No idea who gave him the confidence, but that cherry mashed potato really is delicious.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHERRYPEA_HANDBOOK_ST: Do not let Dave see this, or he may actually throw Jalapenos into the wishing well.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHOMPERBLOW_HANDBOOK_:
Dave fitted Blover's fan blades to Chomper's head and announced that he had invented a fan powered by zombie biomass.
Chomper does not care. As long as there is something to eat, he is happy. “Come straight into my mouth!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHOMPERPOT_HANDBOOK_S: Chomper Pot used to work on another production. He claims to be sick of mushrooms, leaves, flaming flowers, and scraps of clothing bitten from plumbers. He came back here for a change of menu.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHOMPERZ_HANDBOOK_STO: After eating far too many zombies, Chomper's complexion began to match theirs. He is now pestering Cupid-shroom for the latest beauty treatment.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CHOMPER_HANDBOOK_STOR: Chomper was nearly booked to perform his signature act in a little shop of horrors, but his agent took such a large cut that the appearance fell through. Chomper bears no grudge. He merely says it was part of the deal.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_COBCANNON_HANDBOOK_ST: What is Cob Cannon really like? Well... he studied at Harvard and worked for a prominent New York law firm. Everyone knows a single shell can wipe out a huge group of zombies, but the question remains: what fires him up?
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_COFFEEBEANSALE_HANDBO: Many plants wonder how Sale Bean manipulates their prices. He takes a sip of tea and calls it “confidential.” Only he knows the truth: he simply erases the old price and writes a new one in permanent ink.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_COFFEEBEAN_HANDBOOK_S: Coffee Bean: “Hey, folks! Hey, what's happening? Who's there? Hey! Did you see that thing? What thing? Whoa, a lion!” Coffee Bean firmly believes this is how one stays energized.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_COFFEEBLOVER_HANDBOOK: Whenever asked how she energizes other plants, Coffee Blover merely smiles. Then a former neighbor revealed that she grinds coffee late into the night. “That aroma may be the secret... Don't ask how I know. Why do you think I moved?”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_COFFEELEAF_HANDBOOK_S: Rain is rare during the day, but that does not stop Coffee Bean from carrying an umbrella. Only Coffee Umbrella knows that the “canopy” is the reward for a devoted hair-care routine. Hybrid technology? That is beside the point.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_COFFEESHEILD_HANDBOOK:
Shield Coffee Bean's knightly helmet is really his coffee cup. He puts it on his head and raises a barrier around the plants: “Protecting others is a knight's duty!”
Why use a barrier instead of the two shields beside him? Those “shields” are coasters he bought online.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CORNPULTM_HANDBOOK_ST: “Magnetic bomb away!” is Magnetic Kernel-pult's favorite line. No one argues about why he stopped throwing immobilizing rounds, because his arguments are always ironclad.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CORNPULT_HANDBOOK_STO: Kernel-pult is the eldest of three lobber brothers. He is the only one who remembers the others' birthdays—though he never remembers them quite correctly.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CORNROTATER_HANDBOOK_: Kernel Rotor works at an amusement park. His popcorn stand is famous for its unusual service. “He blows the popcorn into your hand—it sounds rude, but it's fun,” says one visitor. “And it tastes so good that I wouldn't mind taking a whole serving to the face.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_CORNTROP_HANDBOOK_STO: Dave spilled a can of buttered kernels over Spikeweed, changing its color and its spikes. It may look like a corn tart now, but zombies can no longer “slip” past so easily.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DAYVASE_HANDBOOK_STOR: “This vase contains a true sun and moon—not the ones in the sky, but younger celestial bodies like them. Less powerful, yet still able to command day and night...” proclaims the old wizard who sells it. If that is true, can he explain why it is mass-produced?
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DIAMONDSEED_HANDBOOK_:
After Dr. Dave cultivated Diamond Seed, a strange man in green clothes and yellow trousers offered an emerald in exchange, saying something about diamond freedom.
“That's right—nine diamonds make a block! Plant them every day and get rich!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DISGUISERBLOVER_HANDB:
This is a drafty piece of cardboard. Bite it and the wind makes your teeth ache.
At least, that is what the zombies think.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DISGUISERCHERRY_HANDB:
Dave forgot the explosives while building a bomb, making Disguised Cherry Bomb furious. “I'm so angry I could explode!”
“...Never mind. I'll explode later.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DISGUISERGATLING_HAND: How does Disguised Gatling Pea work? Is there a gun behind the cardboard, or is a Gatling Pea's soul sealed inside? No one knows. One thing is certain: the gun may be fake, but the bullets are real—and they hurt zombies.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DISGUISERSUNFLOWER_HA: Asked why she looks so much like Sunflower, Disguised Sunflower replies, “Sunflower is my idol, so I worked hard to imitate her. I may have begun as a sheet of cardboard, but I have a heart that follows its dreams.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DOOMCOBCANNON_HANDBOO: Not corn but Doom-shroom; not popcorn but a mushroom cloud. Doom Cannon can never decide which family it belongs to. “I know—mushroom corn soup!” suggests a Peashooter. Is that what Dave ate the other day?
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DOOMSHROOMGAR_HANDBOO: “Transformation or destruction?” murmurs Red-eye Doom-shroom, eyes glowing strangely. “For a zombie, that hardly seems like a choice.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DOOMSHROOM_HANDBOOK_S: “You're lucky I'm on your side,” says Doom-shroom. “I can destroy anything you're afraid of. Piece of cake.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_DOOMTANGLEKELP_HANDBO: Doom Kelp was actually a Doom-shroom all along. He simply fell into the water and became tangled in some kelp.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FEVERBLOVER_HANDBOOK_: Frenzy Blover excels at fanning flames—and at both fanning and flaming. He is wild, loves money, and especially loves hurling it into an enemy's face. His feud with the zombies is simple: one of them picked up a silver coin that should have been his.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FEVERSTAR_HANDBOOK_ST: Frenzy Starfruit does not mind being called “Fire Starfruit.” He loves fire and craves heat; bathing in Jalapeno's flames sends his spirits soaring. For his health, he is considering moving next to Torchwood instead. At least there is still fire there.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FIREDOOMSHROOM_HANDBO: Despite his permanently furious appearance, Flaming Doom-shroom is easy to live with. In fact, he and Ice-shroom share the same ailment. Every weekend they attend physical therapy together for their frozen facial expressions.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FIRENUT_HANDBOOK_STOR: Wall-nut adores fireworks and never tires of them. “The very thought makes my head—and my whole body—burn with excitement!” More than his head may be burning. He seems unaware that nutshells are flammable.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FIRESNOWPEA_HANDBOOK_:
“Let's sleep in the sauna!” “No, the refrigerator!” Frostfire Split Pea argues every night about which room to choose.
“The steam between those two heads really would suit a sauna,” observes Dave.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FIRETALLNUT_HANDBOOK_: Ice Torch Tall-nut plainly has an even tougher post than his brother, yet hides a warm heart beneath his frosty appearance. He likes the nickname “Baked Alaska”—perfect for children who want a frozen dessert and a hot drink at once.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FIREWORK_HANDBOOK_STO:
Happy Lunar New Year 2026!
—A New Year greeting that began in 2025
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FUMESEASHROOM_HANDBOO: Sea Fume-shroom has become self-conscious about his size. “Should I try some exercise besides diving?” he wonders, hoping no one will secretly call him “Big Sea-shroom” again.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FUMESHROOMC_HANDBOOK_: Cherry Fume-shroom suspects she has trouble socializing. “No matter how warmly I treat people, we never get along...” Everyone who spends time with her eventually develops an explosive temper.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_FUMESHROOM_HANDBOOK_S: “My old dead-end job was producing yeast spores for a bakery,” says Fume-shroom. “Then Puff-shroom—bless him—told me about this chance to spray zombies. I feel like a completely different mushroom.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARCOBCANNON_HANDBOOK:
Many plants avoid Zombie Cob Cannon's oppressive presence. From afar, they study his crooked gun carriage and unbowed brow, wondering what battles he has survived...
“I'm only a jar porter,” he says helplessly. “Please stop inventing stories. It's embarrassing...”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARDENSET_HANDBOOK_ST: “Great odds, great prizes—Diamond Seed, Fortune Cat, you name it... Stop! Congratulations, you've won another Garden Set. Care to spin again?” Before regulators stepped in, the vendor reportedly spun plenty of sun out of that routine.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARGANTUARSHROOM_HAND:
Dave supposedly created this plant by capturing a Red-eye Gargantuar. It no longer resembles Hypno-shroom; when eaten, the giant's vengeful spirit possesses the zombie and fights for Dave...
“What are you doing?” asks Peashooter, turning on the light. “That's just a moldy Hypno-shroom!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLICBIRD_HANDBOOK_S: Garlic Bird is the plants' resident mediator, settling disputes with the refrain, “Let it go, let it go—life isn't easy for anyone.” Even zombies heed the advice to take a step back, though no one knows whether they understand or are simply fleeing the smell.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLICBOMB_HANDBOOK_S:
“We're the most poisonous!” says Garlic One. “No, we're the hottest!” argues Garlic Two.
“Forget it. Let's not act like those cherries and quarrel over something so trivial.” Agreement at last.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLICCHOMPER_HANDBOO: Garlic Chomper always smells as if he just left an Italian restaurant. His motto is “Aroma is strength,” though it keeps neighboring plants at a distance. When they ask him to sunbathe elsewhere, he cheerfully calls the odor a natural social-distancing tool.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLICJALAPENO_HANDBO: “Can you believe it? I taste of garlic, and even my flames smell of garlic. That's why the zombies all run from me,” says Garlic Jalapeno. Fortunately, the plants still accept him.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLICPOT_HANDBOOK_ST: Plants standing in Garlic Pot would rather change lanes than the zombies; his odor is overwhelming. “Hold on! Zombies hate garlic, so they can't get past me,” he insists, forgetting that zombies take a bite of everything they meet.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLICTALLNUT_HANDBOO: Asked how garlic genes drive zombies away, Garlic Tall-nut replies, “I don't use garlic genes. My imposing Tall-nut build frightens them off. At most I use a little allicin and carry a faint garlic scent. What? Why is my head pointed? Well, let me ask you...”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GARLIC_HANDBOOK_STORY: Changing lanes is not merely Garlic's profession; it is his passion. He earned a doctorate in directional studies from Brussels University and can lecture all day about route vectors and counterattack arrays. He even rearranges his furniture into the street. How does his wife put up with it?
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GATLINGCABBAGE_HANDBO: “Honestly, I envy how the cabbages attack freely over uneven ground,” admits Gatling Pea. So he traded techniques with Cabbage-pult, though his own attack style never changed completely.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GATLINGCAT_HANDBOOK_S: “Military helmet? Threw it away ages ago. Dave calls this ‘tactical cuteness.’ My firing rate is apparently up twenty percent, so it really works.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GATLINGPEA_HANDBOOK_S: When Gatling Pea enlisted, his parents worried. “Darling, it's too dangerous,” they said together. He refused to compromise. “Life itself is dangerous,” he replied, eyes shining with steely resolve.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GATLINGPOT_HANDBOOK_S: Gatling Pot was ordinary until he acquired a Gatling costume. “One lucky pull!” he boasts. Everyone might have believed him if they had not seen the same outfit discounted in the store.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GATLINGZ_HANDBOOK_STO: “Listen, little brother,” Zombie Gatling Pea tells the confused Zombie Peashooter in a surprisingly commanding voice. “Whether we're zombies or plants doesn't matter. What matters is our true purpose—we fight for ‘brains’ either way, don't we?”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GHOSTBUSTER_HANDBOOK_: Plants affectionately call Ghost Devourer “the emergency line.” Besides loving kittens, he finds new employment for Zombie Ghosts released from rehabilitation.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GIFTMACHINE_HANDBOOK_: “Arcades always have flashy little contraptions—like this prize machine,” says Dave. “Crazy...” Hot Dog Shooter does not mention that it secretly put the taco inside. Who wants to watch a poor old man leave the casino empty-handed?
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GLOOMPULT_HANDBOOK_ST: A strange illness gave Gloom-shroom a tail, so the other plants mistake him for a lobber. Only he knows he remains a mushroom. Perhaps that is why he is so gloomy.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GLOOMSHROOM_HANDBOOK_: “I love releasing great clouds of fumes,” says Gloom-shroom. “Some people can't stand it; they call it vulgar. Well, would they rather have zombies chewing on their skulls?”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GLOOMSQUASH_HANDBOOK_:
Gloom Squash has been inexplicably furious lately.
“I'm terribly agitated. They say it's what happens when a Squash gets too gloomy.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GOLDCAT_HANDBOOK_STOR:
He learned his technique in an ancient kingdom—something called Throw Gil, perhaps? Cats like him supposedly end up round as balls.
“None of that matters. I'm the richest cat alive! Who cares if I get fat?”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GOLDHAMMER_HANDBOOK_S:
“I need your help!” says Golden Hammer. “Fill just three more craters and you'll earn a gold card!”
Somehow, the counter always gets stuck at 3.999999...
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GOLDMAGNET_HANDBOOK_S:
Gold Magnet once complained all day: about a wasted life, a lost office, and automatic collection stealing the one lawn job he did well. After a perilous hybrid adventure and a hard-won return home, he finally learned the value of a quiet life.
“Ooh—wait, a coin!” And money. He still loves money.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GOLDMELONPULT_HANDBOO:
“Is that rind made of gold, or are the seeds gold?”
“Funny you should ask. Both.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GOLDPEA_HANDBOOK_STOR: People often mistake Gold Magnet Shooter for a banana. It is actually Gold Magnet's shooter form. While gaming late at night, it can often be heard yelling, “Seriously, bro?!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GRAVEBOMBER_HANDBOOK_: Why did the once-gentle Grave Buster become as frightening as he looks? “My anger isn't directed at you—only at the zombies' illegal construction,” says Grave Bomber. Later everyone learned that the spreading graves had forced both his favorite cat café and convalescent home to relocate.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GRAVEBUSTERG_HANDBOOK: “A gentleman acquires wealth by honorable means,” says Treasure Devourer, pointing into the golden pit. “As for where those means lie, I've shown you the way.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GRAVEBUSTER_HANDBOOK_: Despite his frightening appearance, Grave Buster wants everyone to know that he loves kittens and volunteers at a zombie rehabilitation center. “I'm only doing the right thing,” he says.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GRAVEMINE_HANDBOOK_ST:
“Every time! Why am I always the one clearing weeds?”
“Take me along next time,” Potato Mine tells Grave Buster. “Then you won't have to clear the same spot twice.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_GWC_HANDBOOK_STORY: Dogtail believes he is stronger than Cattail. “My incredible nose lets me identify and attack zombies!” He forgets that during a huge wave, the smell comes from every direction.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HAMBURGER_HANDBOOK_ST: Burger Shooter hates arguments over rival fast-food fandoms. He simply stays true to himself: “Fighting zombies is my duty, but burgers are my eternal faith.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HAMMERLIGHT_HANDBOOK_: Glow Hammer is merely a conveniently shaped piece of wood. Still, Dave believes in using whatever is at hand, so he plugs craters with it. “Surprisingly good balance.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HOTDOG_HANDBOOK_STORY: “Butter, corn, peas...” mutters Hot Dog Shooter. This is not his year-end report; it is the taco recipe. Supplying tacos to Dave's house is the rear-facing shooter's main responsibility.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HURTTALLNUT_HANDBOOK_: “Yes, we're injured, and no, we don't object to active duty.” Injured Tall-nut adjusts his bandages. “I'm delighted to be useful somewhere other than as a construction-site load-bearing wall.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HWC_HANDBOOK_STORY: Foxtail is immensely proud of her tails; ordinary foxes have only one. She dreams of growing nine and becoming an immortal of legend. Sage sometimes points out that she is not really a fox, but Foxtail pretends not to hear.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOBEAN_HANDBOOK_ST: “Yes, everyone prefers to call me an idol,” says Hypno Coffee Bean. “I can't sing or dance, but I'm irresistible—perhaps because I can manufacture fans?”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOBLOVER_HANDBOOK_: Hypno Blover calls herself “Little Sister.” She and several enthusiasts in the hypno family supposedly became sworn sisters. She is actually older than both “elder” sisters, but was too dizzy from spinning to remember her age.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNODOOMSHROOM_HANDB: Rumors surround Hypno Doom-shroom's origin, but there was no sinister laboratory or regrettable romance. Clumsy Doom-shroom simply knocked over some paint and splattered it over the zombies when he exploded.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOGARLIC_HANDBOOK_: Garlic once worked in a paint factory, the only place that concealed his smell. One day a clumsy fellow spilled the paint, costing Garlic his job and leaving him brightly colored.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOPATCH_HANDBOOK_S: As the star of the hypno circuit, Hypno-shroom Patch welcomes every zombie admirer. She loves showing off her “fans” to the other mushrooms, though the mindless fellows always wander away eventually.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOSHROOMGHOST_HAND: Everyone knew Phantom Hypno-shroom only as the owner of an amusement-park haunted house—until she walked onto the lawn with giant enforcers and calmly faced the horde. “Mafia? I just felt unsafe and hired some guards,” says a languid voice beneath the mask. No one believes she is quite so simple anymore.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOSHROOMICE_HANDBO:
Ice-cold composure defines Ice Torch Hypno-shroom. Rumor says she has become rather hot lately...
“Achoo!” Apparently she is simply delirious with fever.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOSHROOMSHOOTER_HA:
Hypno-shroom always dreamed of becoming a messenger of love, so she dressed as her idol, Cupid, and vowed to bring love and happiness to every zombie.
Gargantuars included!
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOSHROOMSUN_HANDBO: Sun Hypno-shroom upholds the family creed: “Zombies are our friends and play an important ecological role. Look,” she says proudly, pointing at a hypnotized zombie, “I've already taught them photosynthesis!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_HYPNOSHROOM_HANDBOOK_: “Zombies are our friends,” insists Hypno-shroom. “They play an important role in our ecosystem. We should work harder to teach them to think the way we do.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICEBOMB_HANDBOOK_STOR: Dave was reportedly injured while taking Cherry Bomb out of the freezer. His doctors are still arguing over whether the wound is frostbite or a burn.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICECACTUS_HANDBOOK_ST: “It's only a cold! I'm just sneezing. Why are you looking at me like that?” says Ice Cactus. “Desert nights get extremely cold, you know!”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICECOBCANNON_HANDBOOK: Every plant envies Ice Cob Cannon's power and speculates about its source; some even suspect modifications. Only he knows that his original goal was simply to eat chilled popcorn.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICEKING_HANDBOOK_STOR: “Ice never decays” is the blessing of Ice-shroom King's crown. To many plants, a crown means supreme authority and power. The King hates his: his icy spikes trap it so perfectly that he cannot remove it to wash his hair.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICENUT_HANDBOOK_STORY: After leaving the freezer, Wall-nut hurriedly put on several extra layers. He had not expected the clothes to freeze too...
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESEASHROOM_HANDBOOK: Sea Ice-shroom constantly stresses the difference between “sea ice” and “sea infantry,” but no one understands. “Listen: he's a marine, I'm Sea Ice-shroom. We are not the same!” Perhaps they only pretend, because everyone enjoys watching him pout when angry.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESHROOM_HANDBOOK_ST: Ice-shroom always frowns—not from unhappiness or disapproval, but because a childhood trauma left his expression permanently frozen.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESPEARPEA_HANDBOOK_: Icicle Shooter is a famous mountaineering influencer. Every crystal on him supposedly comes from a different summit, a natural medal. Skeptics call it marketing: “Even if it's true, that's no excuse to face the camera without washing for days.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESQUASH_HANDBOOK_ST: This is what Squash became after two thousand years trapped in a freezer. How did he return to the present? Beside him, we found a fragment of a time machine.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESTINKY_HANDBOOK_ST: The snail has no special talent. It simply works harder than everyone else.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESUNMINE_HANDBOOK_S: Frostlight Potato Mine is an important member of the Sun Club, but remains too “cool” for anyone to notice. He plans to dye his icicles so zombies mistake him for shaved ice and approach willingly.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_ICESUNSHROOM_HANDBOOK: Frostlight-shroom is a great scientist who converts zombies' internal energy into solar power. His steadily receding hairline troubles him. “Research demands sacrifice,” he tells himself.

TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNFLOWERZ_HANDBOOK_S: The last zombie to eat Sunflower became full and left part unfinished. When the unlucky plant recovered, she grew back looking like a zombie.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNFLOWER_HANDBOOK_ST: Sunflower cannot resist dancing to a beat. What beat? The earth's own energizing jazz rhythm, at a frequency only Sunflowers can hear.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNGODBEAN_HANDBOOK_S:
“The divine commanded light, and I was born. I bestow the sun equally upon creation, and all things dance in praise—”
“Enough up there! You're too bright for us to sleep!” interrupt the mushrooms.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNMINE_HANDBOOK_STOR: Sun Bomb was not the first to extract sunlight from zombies. “There was no plagiarism,” says Sun Potato Mine. “I founded the Sun Club; she joined it.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNPAD_HANDBOOK_STORY: Solar Lily Pad claims to embody sunlight: “I warm plants and barbecue approaching zombies!” Balancing heat is difficult. He turns himself down to avoid burns and cannot even boil the pool nearby.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNPEASHOOTER_HANDBOO: The first pea-family member of the Sun Club is proud of the distinction. “Most members forget that sunlight does more than grow plants. It carries tremendous heat.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNPOT_HANDBOOK_STORY: Sun Pot stares straight upward. “Don't misunderstand; it's simply noon,” she says. Hopefully the excuse will still hide her stiff neck tonight.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNPULT_HANDBOOK_STOR: Throwing one's own brothers seems strange even in a world where Melon-pult throws melons. “They're only plastic replicas,” explains Sun-shroom-pult. He bought the basket from Cabbage-pult too.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SUNSHROOM_HANDBOOK_ST: Sun-shroom hates sunlight so much that it spits out every trace produced inside its body. It simply cannot tolerate the stuff.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_SWC_HANDBOOK_STORY: Sage is not a real mouse, but has long feuded with Cattail. “I avoid that barking creature whenever possible, yet those awful zombies force us to fight together.” In some timeline, Dogtail may have lived with them too.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TABOOBEAN_HANDBOOK_ST: “I am not exploiting them. Under my command, they shine,” says Taboo Coffee Bean, swirling a glass of red wine.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TABOODOOMSHROOM_HANDB: Taboo Doom-shroom's explosion is not infinitely powerful. Before the smoke clears, he drags zombies underground. “No one will discover my trick,” he boasts, forgetting to fill the hole.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TALLNUTARMED_HANDBOOK: “To withstand zombies, one must be strong and fully armored,” says Armored Tall-nut. “And carry spare revival scrolls.” He avoids magnetic plants in case they steal his armor.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TALLNUTPS_HANDBOOK_ST: Nobody knows why Primal Spikerock Nut looks this way. “Evolution tested us in the harshest conditions,” he sighs, unwilling to recall millions of years spent smashed by giants, trampled by dinosaurs, and rammed by zombies.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TALLNUTUMBRELLA_HANDB: “Boom! I spread my leaves to repel threats from above and ladders placed against me,” says Umbrella Tall-nut, tossing his leafy “hair.” “This is how I protect my neighbors. Trust me.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TALLNUT_HANDBOOK_STOR: Are Wall-nut and Tall-nut rivals? Tall-nut laughs in a deep baritone. “Rivals? We're friends. Do you know what Wall-nut once did for me...” His voice trails off into a sly smile.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TANGLEKELPH_HANDBOOK_: Underwater kelp is deceptive: drowning swimmers think it cannot hold them, often tragically. “I feel sorry for them. They only swim forward, so I let them go again.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TANGLEKELP_HANDBOOK_S: “I'm completely invisible,” thinks Tangle Kelp. “No one sees me below the surface.” Friends insist they see him clearly, but he refuses to believe them.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREECACTUS_HANDBOOK_: Three-Cactus prefers steady teamwork. Even tiny breezes combined can push zombies back. He merely has to endure Cactus Blover's grumbling.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREECORNPULT_HANDBOO: Kernel-pult is eldest of three lobbers and alone remembers their birthdays—badly. He now keeps three baskets of notes so their important dates no longer get mixed up.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREEHYBIRDPEATER_HAN: An early hybrid, Hybrid Threepeater is respected by the pea family. “They say we symbolize pea unity,” says the Repeater head. “True enough—we peas stick together as tightly as us.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREEPEATERG_HANDBOOK: Garlic Threepeater hopes to enter the third Hybrid Plant Beauty Pageant, believing pale complexions hide every flaw. “Forget it,” cough the zombies, holding their noses.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREEPEATERU_HANDBOOK: Rebirth by fire usually ends in transformation or ash, but sometimes takes a stranger turn. “Is this still my world?” asks Blazing Threepeater, studying the familiar yet foreign lawn in new phoenix plumage. A new legend begins.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREEPEATERZ_HANDBOOK: Zombie Threepeater is the plant-zombie team's strategist—not through brilliance, but because the others believe three foolish heads together make one wise adviser.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_THREEPEATER_HANDBOOK_: Threepeater enjoys books, chess, parks, and modern jazz concerts. “I'm searching for my other half,” he says. His favorite number is five.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TORCHWOODSTAR_HANDBOO: One mighty projectile deals great damage—but a spark starts a wildfire. Countless small stars together create overwhelming force. That is Starfruit Torchwood's creed.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TORCHWOODZ_HANDBOOK_S: By instinct, Zombie Torchwood believes plants and zombies are one family. “There are no enemies here. Attacking either side feels wrong.” So he joins one, hoping to convert the other later.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TORCHWOOD_HANDBOOK_ST: Everyone admires Torchwood's honesty, loyal friendship, and ability to strengthen peas. Yet he hides an unspeakable secret: he cannot read.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TWINKABBAGE_HANDBOOK_: Twin Taco Cattail seems strangely familiar to everyone. “We're surprised too,” says the cabbage head. “I expected to remain a spirit behind him until the gentleman in the saucepan ordered a double taco.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_TWINSUNSHROOM_HANDBOO: “Pea Sunflower was mad enough, but I never imagined becoming an experiment myself!” Twin Sunflower says whenever Twin Sunflower-shroom appears. Even experimental results can become new experimental material.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_UMBRELLATORCH_HANDBOO: “Pudding? Sweet rice dumplings?” Torch Umbrella blinks during his daily hair care. “What are those? They sound delicious.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_UMBRELLLEAF_HANDBOOK_: “Boom! Like that? I can do it again. Boom! I snap my leaves upward to protect my neighbors. Yes! Exactly. Trust me,” says Leaf Umbrella.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_UPGRADEBEAN_HANDBOOK_: Upgrade Bean loves festive cheer and wears this outfit every Lunar New Year, wishing everyone a promotion, a raise, and overflowing prosperity.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_VIPNUT_HANDBOOK_STORY: The most self-sacrificing nut received a crown after countless bandaging procedures. “I feel mightier than every nut!” says VIP Nut. “Careful with the wire!” someone calls—he is playing the sun in a theater.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUSHOOTER_HANDBOO: “I meant to produce Wall-nuts,” says Wall-nut Bowling. “Mine simply cannot stand. Thank goodness they still help the front line.” Other plants disagree; rolling nuts flatten their leaves and stems.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUTABC_HANDBOOK_S: Wall-nut fell in love with Russian culture and coats. “One more layer!” Why can he afford only two? Ask Piggy-bank Nut.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUTHOLE_HANDBOOK_: How is Pit Nut's hat made? “A little soil, 9.55 ounces of fertilizer, and a fragment of the fourth dimension,” he explains. Doom-shroom scoffs.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUTSALE_HANDBOOK_: Sale Wall-nut spent three dollars improving his packaging. A week later, he launched the same promotion for the thirty-third time: buy one, get one free.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUTSQUASH_HANDBOO: Squash Nut and Potato Mine are childhood friends. “I prepare completely and strike at the last moment!” says Squash Nut. Potato Mine agrees, though he dislikes the tingling back massages zombies provide.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUTZ_HANDBOOK_STO: “People wonder why these zombies cannot infect anyone. Allow me to clarify.” Somewhere, a Wall-nut remembers an older life as a walnut shell.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WALLNUT_HANDBOOK_STOR: “What does being chewed feel like? My limited senses register only a tingle, like a relaxing back massage.”
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WILDPEA_HANDBOOK_STOR: The fiercest Gatling Pea rains fire like meteors. Incidentally, his helmet is a shrub from next door's front yard, and the cape is their bedsheet.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WINTERMELONCAT_HANDBO: Winter Melon Cattail dreamed of becoming an ice princess. She nearly succeeded until she donned a frozen gown and barked with excitement.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WINTERMELONPULTX_HAND: Legend places Arctic Winter Melon's origin in the far north. Actually, he grew up in a country well, then came to a chilled-melon club and entered the wrong freezer compartment.
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WINTERMELONPULT_HANDB: Winter Melon tries to calm his frayed nerves as zombie footsteps approach. Can he manage it? Can anyone?
TOWERDEFENSE_PLANT_WINTERMELONSHROOM_HAN: A striped winter-melon cap made Fume-shroom unique. Every mushroom marvels at the chill beneath his cap... Oh no, he is about to sneeze. Take cover!
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_AIRCRAFT_HANDBOOK_ST:
Aircraft Zombie enters a hardware store. “One huge balloon, a metal frame, rope, a propeller with motor, and thick paint.”
“That will be expensive, sir.”
“Charge it to Blover.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ALIEN_HANDBOOK_STORY: A zombie from the PC2009 galaxy. Aliens have little interest in human brains; they are obsessed with brainlight and need it as an energy source. Have they come to the wrong place?
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ANGEL_HANDBOOK_STORY: Nobody knows whether zombie angels exist. This fellow is merely unlucky: his clothes vanished while he showered, so he grabbed a theatrical costume instead.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ARMORED_GARGANTUARRE: The zombies praise Armored Red-eye Gargantuar and his equipment as the highest glory. “With gear like this, who needs a girlfriend?” he shouts to cheers. No one sees him weep alone at night.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ARMORED_GARGANTUAR_H: Gargantuars are elite zombies; a fully armed Gargantuar is the elite of the elite. Yet he remains unhappy, because all that equipment cannot help him find a girlfriend.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_AXE_HANDBOOK_STORY: Hatchet Zombie became obsessed with the bandit heroes of Water Margin and imitates the twin-axe warrior Li Kui. Only one axe in his hands? Ask Magnet-shroom where the other went.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BACKUPDANCER_HANDBOO: Backup Dancer Zombie studied dance for six years at the Chewilliard School of Performing Arts in Zombie New York City.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BACKUPGARGANTUAR_HAN: Backup Dancer Gargantuar is Berserk Dancing Gargantuar's most devoted giant-groupie. Rumor says both grew big by eating brains.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BACKUPPAPER_HANDBOOK: Disco Zombie's backup dancers remain loyal even in retirement. Whenever their leader calls, they rush in to show every offender the fury of a senior dance crew.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BACKUP_HANDBOOK_STOR: Dancer Zombie studied dance for four years at the Chewilliard School of Performing Arts in Zombie New York City.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BALLOONBOMB_HANDBOOK: Is this what they mean by trouble falling from the sky?
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BALLOONCOLOUR_HANDBO: Colorful Balloon Zombie collects balloons from parks and fairs. They fascinate him as much as brains. When his precious balloons burst, he rushes to leave—without noticing that he is flying the wrong way.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BALLOONJACKSON_HANDB: Balloon Zombie is lucky; few zombies find balloons. The Dancing Zombie riding above is luckier still—not every celebrity arrives by private aircraft.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BALLOONPULT_HANDBOOK: Perhaps the plants really do need a balloon-popping monkey.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BALLOON_HANDBOOK_STO: Balloon Zombie is lucky. Balloons have many uses, and few other zombies have ever found one.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BED_HANDBOOK_STORY: The Doctor recently borrowed an idea from a game: he brainwashed a zombie into loving sleep and skiing—even though there is no snow here.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BOSS_HANDBOOK_STORY: George Edgar Zomboss earned a doctorate in Thanatology in only two years and swiftly mastered its technology. He built a terrifying giant zombie mech and began establishing a local dictatorship.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BUCKETHEAD_HANDBOOK_: Buckethead Zombie's paint bucket makes him stand out in a cold, uncaring world. In truth, he simply forgot it was still on his head.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BUNGIBIN_HANDBOOK_ST: Need an unwanted plant collected? Call Trash Can Bungee Zombie! He arrives uninvited and considers everything old—including your brain.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_BUNGI_HANDBOOK_STORY: Bungee Zombie loves danger. Once you are no longer alive, what harm is there in experiencing death again?
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CABBAGEPULT_HANDBOOK: Cabbage-pult Zombie is good at pelting plants with cabbages and makes a living from it. He still cannot understand how plants suddenly appear in front of him.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CAPTAIN_HANDBOOK_STO: Legend says his airborne pirate ship drops crew on command. Actually, he arranged the entrance over drinks with Bungee Zombies. His real ship was impounded for illegal parking.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CATAPOW_HANDBOOK_STO: Rocket Artillery Zombie rebuilt his vehicle from hoarded scrap. The new cannon fires anything with four times the efficiency and accuracy, yet repeated tests confirm that basketballs remain ideal ammunition.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CATAPULT_HANDBOOK_ST: Catapult Zombie can launch virtually anything, but basketballs seem to be the perfect ammunition.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CAT_HANDBOOK_STORY: Cat Warrior Zombie never removes his mask. “I am a cat. A cat reacts seven times faster than a zombie.” As a devoted carnivore, he believes this helps him avoid unappetizing plants.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CHESS_HANDBOOK_STORY: Chinese Checkers Zombie is a veteran player and placed second in the last Zombie Chess Championship. Before checkmate, the champion ate the board; the judges unanimously praised this as exceptionally “zombie.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CHOMPER_HANDBOOK_STO: Chomper Zombie calls himself a gourmet. Nibbling plants or brains lacks flavor; frantic gnawing lacks elegance. Only swallowing them whole and chewing slowly preserves the full taste with proper refinement. Other zombies cannot imitate him—their mouths are too small.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_COBCANNON_HANDBOOK_S: Besides brains, Cob Cannon Zombie loves popcorn. Unfortunately, he does not know how it is cooked, so he blasts things at random according to his “instincts.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CONEHEAD_HANDBOOK_ST: Conehead Zombie once marched blindly forward like all the others. Then something made him stop, pick up a traffic cone, and fasten it to his head. Yes—he loves parties.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CORNPULT_HANDBOOK_ST: Kernel-pult Zombie feels top-heavy, so he throws away kernels one at a time. He hopes to make his head lighter—and clearer—so there is room to remember his brothers' birthdays.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_CREW_HANDBOOK_STORY: “A ship cannot go one day without a master,” agree the Pirate Crew Zombies. If their captain falls, rock-paper-scissors immediately elects a successor to inherit his position, ideals, hat, and fake beard.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DANCERFIRE_HANDBOOK_: Flame Dancers are adolescents; their mustaches are fake. They dyed their flames green to frame the lead dancer's yellow fire. “I never wanted to dye this thing green!”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DARKFOOTBALL_HANDBOO: As captain, Dark Football Zombie brings 300 percent enthusiasm to every game. He understands offense and defense perfectly, though he still does not understand football.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DIAMOND_HANDBOOK_STO: Diamond Zombie was the town's famously wealthy heir. Unwilling to look cheap and rotten after death, he had his fortune buried beside him. Even now, he can dress very expensively.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DIGGERGATLINGPEA_HAN: Digger Zombie heard that mining was dangerous and that four-legged exploding monsters lurked below, so he carried a Gatling gun. The tunnels were too dark to fire safely; he decided to wait until he reached the surface.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DIGGER_HANDBOOK_STOR: Digger Zombie spends three days every week applying for excavation permits.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DIGGER_POTATOMINE_HA: Hearing that miners feared four-legged exploding monsters, Digger Zombie dressed as one to frighten his coworkers. Unfortunately, he mistook a real mine for the prop.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DISCOFIRE_HANDBOOK_S: “Fire isn't dangerous, friend. I stand safely inside the inner flame,” boasts Flame Disco Zombie. “Now we're really on fire!”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DISCOGARGANTUAR_HAND: The legendary zombie superstar has both brains and brawn—or at least brawn and dance. Following Disco Zombie's glamorous steps, will this giant finally find a partner?
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DISCOPAPER_HANDBOOK_: Tea, newspapers, and quiet walks: the former star has faded into an ordinary old man. “I'm tired of glittering excess. It is time to enjoy a peaceful life of my own.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DISCO_HANDBOOK_STORY: Disco Zombie's latest record, Grab That Brain and Bite, Bite, Bite, is rocketing up the zombie charts.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DOLPHINDC_HANDBOOK_S: “Pink is the color of real men!” the Backup Dancer Dolphin Zombies reply when asked about their dolphins. It is easy to be confident when the pink belongs to the mount.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DOLPHINMJ_HANDBOOK_S: Perfect Dancing Zombie fashion and a brilliant aquatic performance earned Dancing Dolphin Zombie rave reviews. The only flaw: the lighting crew struggled to keep up with the dolphin.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DOLPHINRIDER_HANDBOO: The dolphin is a zombie too.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DOLPHINSN_HANDBOOK_S: Dolphin Knight borrowed scuba gear to ride underwater. There was no spare mask for the dolphin, but he is unconcerned. Dolphins need air, certainly—but this dolphin is a zombie.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DOOMSHROOM_HANDBOOK_: “Bad luck: this time I'm not on your side,” says Doom-shroom Zombie. “I can effortlessly destroy everything you treasure.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DUCKRIDER_HANDBOOK_S: Duck Rider assembled his mount from stolen equipment and happily gives others a lift—unless they call it a duck. He thinks it is an ostrich.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_DUCK_HANDBOOK_STORY: “Why the pigtails?” zombies constantly ask Rubber Duck Zombie. He offers little explanation, believing childhood innocence is precious. Unfortunately, he often forgets to bring his rubber-duck float home.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FARMER_HANDBOOK_STOR: Farmer Zombie adores the card game Happy Brain Landlords, though losing streaks often leave him owing several buckets of brains.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FATGOLD_HANDBOOK_STO: Tycoon Zombie is a mystery. However much money he drops, his savings never visibly shrink; however hard he diets, neither does his waistline. Both rank among zombiekind's great unsolved questions.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FIRENUT_HANDBOOK_STO: After watching Flame Dancing Zombie, Torch-nut Zombie began an awkward imitation. Unfortunately, he cannot attract a single fan.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FLAG_HANDBOOK_STORY: Flag Zombie unquestionably loves brains, but privately he is equally fascinated by flags. Perhaps that is because his flag has a brain painted on it. Hard to say.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLBLACK_FUMESH: Apparently turning dark really does double one's power: stronger armor, greater combat strength, and connections on the black football team. The drawback? Spending time with teammates who know no rules made him forget football too.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLBLACK_GLOOMS: Will nobody tell him that spore weapons violate the rules? Then again, no zombie has ever understood the rules—or even what football is.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLGARGANTUARBL: The Black Giant Team is an all-star institution. A director is preparing a promotional film rumored to be titled Black Football: Gargantuar.
This heavyweight rarely appears in public and is absent even from the team film. Rumor says he will appear in the Black Football: Gargantuar DLC. Nobody knows if it is true.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLGARGANTUAR_H: Charging Football Gargantuar always leads from the front, his enormous body radiating pressure. Only he knows the truth: he cannot play football at all.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLIMPBLACKWHIT: Faster and stronger, Charging Black Football Imp instantly draws every eye. After endless effort, he has finally become today's center of attention—look, they are throwing him like a football again!
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLIMPBLACK_HAN: Rumor says this is merely an Imp with conjunctivitis and no extra power. That does not stop him serving as Red-eye Black Football Gargantuar's personal assistant—and spare football.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALLIMP_HANDBOOK: Charging Football Imp is an agile zombie celebrity who dodges every collision. His one complaint: when Gargantuar passes to a teammate, he gets overexcited and throws the Imp instead of the ball.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALL_FUMESHROOM_: “One day you'll all be my fans! Faster, stronger, unstoppable—the field's newest star!” cries Fume-shroom Football Zombie. Nobody answers; the spores are already as thick as his enthusiasm.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALL_GLOOMSHROOM: “I'm protecting everyone,” explains Gloom-shroom Football Zombie. “Plant fire is intense, so I make fog to block their view.” Nobody tells him that plants can detect zombies through fog.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_FOOTBALL_HANDBOOK_ST: Football Zombie brings 110 percent passion to the field. He cooperates, attacks, and defends expertly, despite having no idea what football is.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARDENER_HANDBOOK_ST: Gardener Zombie grows nothing; he only carries plants. Rumor claims his diligence is for the “class flower” he remembers. A pun started the rumor: that empty head thinks only of “carrying flowers.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUARDIAMOND_HA: Diamond Gargantuar is unquestionably zombie society's most eligible diamond bachelor. The plants prefer calling him a sneaky menace.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUARDIGGER_HAN: Quiet and aloof, Digger Gargantuar always appears where needed, earning every zombie's trust. Only he knows why he never reaches the objective: he has been reading the blueprint backward again.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUARZOMBONIRED: Red-eye Gargantuar saved for ages to buy a new Zomboni. “He even talks about that ‘world's coolest car’ in his sleep,” says his Imp partner. “I can't bear to tell him everyone owns that model.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUARZOMBONI_HA: A retired Zomboni taught Gargantuar everything he knew and commissioned a giant ice machine just for him.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUAR_GLOOMPULT: Gloom-pult Gargantuar is the gloomiest zombie alive. He broods over his own failed courtship and the romantic history of his whole family. Only attacking plants lets him vent the gloom.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUAR_HANDBOOK_: The ground shakes when Gargantuar walks. Other zombies fall silent when he laments. He is everything they dream of becoming—yet still has no girlfriend.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUAR_PRESENTBO: Gargantuar and Imp exchange Christmas presents. Gargantuar put his gift where Imp would instantly see it—on his own head. Imp had the same idea. Now neither can see the other's surprise.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUAR_REDEYE_HA: “Red-eye Giant” is Berserk Gargantuar's other name. He is a colossal zombie with power every zombie envies... and still no girlfriend.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GARGANTUAR_WALLNUTZ_: Zombie Wall-nut Gargantuar longs to join the zombie family, but they distrust him. “He has no brain like us, but he's too wooden—literally. Does he even know whether he's smashing plants or zombies?”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GATLINGDOLPHINRIDER_: Nobody knows why the dolphin is undead—not even Gatling Dolphin Zombie. He has carried it since his adventures began while seeking both its origins and his helmet's. They were birthday gifts from other zombies; he forgot.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GATLINGPEA_HANDBOOK_: Gatling Zombie is furious. Once uniquely imposing, he has watched more and more zombies acquire Gatling guns. To restore his prestige, he is researching an even stronger wild model.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_GHOST_HANDBOOK_STORY: In life, he spent years researching immortality without noticing that he was already undead—a zombie.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_HYPNOTIST_HANDBOOK_S: Why does he remain so long? He hypnotized himself too.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_HYPNO_HANDBOOK_STORY: Mesmerized Zombie never seems fully awake. If you see him wandering and yawning, stay twice as alert—or his condition may prove contagious.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ICENUT_HANDBOOK_STOR: Ice Nut Zombie heard of a nut on the plant side who became a “God of War.” Excited, he climbed into a freezer to imitate him, overlooking one detail: he is not a Tall-nut Zombie.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ICETALLNUT_HANDBOOK_: Ice Tall-nut Zombie has never understood heat. Perhaps his brain contains no concept of warmth. Wait—he has no brain.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPCLOUD_HANDBOOK_ST: Cloud Imps are especially irritating. They circle overhead, chatter, and throw things. If they swarm you, seek help from someone—perhaps a legendary plumber.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPDIAMOND_HANDBOOK_: When Gargantuar struck it rich, he naturally gave the little brother who shared his hardships a dazzling new outfit too.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPDIGGERSPIKE_HANDB: Imp recently played a game called PvZ Hybrid and became fascinated by combining things. He fused mining equipment with Spikeweed and calls it cosplay, though he cannot explain what he is cosplaying.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPDIGGER_HANDBOOK_S: As site foreman, he receives three more brain biscuits at afternoon tea than an ordinary Digger Zombie.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPHACKER_HANDBOOK_S: Hacker Imp keeps a low profile offline so nobody suspects his computer expertise. Despite infiltrating countless machines, his favorite target remains the homeowner's brain.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPPULT_HANDBOOK_STO: Catapult Zombie promised to help the Imps rehearse an aerial act on the weekend. Evidently, he forgot to unload them before basketball practice.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPSCAREDY_HANDBOOK_: Coward Imp remembers his first night on the lawn: a tall, top-heavy mushroom stared, then suddenly folded up like a beetle spreading its wings. Terrified, he copied the mushroom's defensive posture, though he remains just as afraid of it.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPSKELETON_HANDBOOK: Skeleton Imp and Skeleton Gargantuar are inseparable. “We're practically one person!” He does not know that he was assembled from his brother's leftover bones.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMPSNAIL_HANDBOOK_ST: Snail Imp is a true homebody who retreats into his shell to enjoy solitude. He also sings, though he knows only one children's song about a grapevine.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_HANDBOOK_STORY: Imp is small but sturdy, trained in zombie judo, zombie karate, and zombie bare-knuckle fighting. He also plays harmonica.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_HYPNOSHROOM_HAND: “We should teach plants to think our way; they are essential to our ecosystem,” Hypno-shroom Imp tells the others in a solemn voice. Nobody cares. Zomboss praises his intelligence, but the horde preferred his old mindless grin.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_PEASHOOTERSINGLE: Peashooter Imp believes he has an advantage over ordinary pea zombies, yet remains self-conscious about his height. He records every suspected insult in a diary that is now nearly taller than he is.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_PEASHOOTERZ_HAND: Zombie Peashooter Imp can never decide which way his head belongs. He feels top-heavy, as if every trace of pigment in his body migrated upward.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_PRESENTBOX_HANDB: Imp meant to prepare Gargantuar a Christmas present, but the box became stuck on his head. He asks his brother for help, yet Gargantuar does not seem to see him. Why?
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_PUFFSHROOM_HANDB: “Roots are a plant's weak point, and we're exactly the right height to strike them. Therefore, we're powerful!” boasts Puff-shroom Imp. Zomboss smiles and sends them to the front to compare theory with practice.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_SEASHROOM_HANDBO: Sea-shroom Imp longs for an ocean he has never seen and follows Sharks, Sirens, and Pirates to hear their grand stories. Whether those storytellers have really seen the sea no longer matters.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_SUNPULT_HANDBOOK: Plants may find throwing one's brother strange. Sun-shroom-pult Imp does not; Imps are thrown by their brothers all the time. Besides, how could that mushroom projectile be related to a zombie?
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_IMP_SUNSHROOM_HANDBO: “Why mourn growing up? A bigger head, a sunnier smile—and I'll finally pass the game's age restrictions legitimately,” says Sun-shroom Imp.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_JACKBOX_HANDBOOK_STO: This zombie shakes not because he is cold, but because he is insane.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_JACKSONX_HANDBOOK_ST: Elite Dancing Zombie defines a generation of zombie pop. Countless dancers dream of following him. When he steps onto the lawn, a grand performance begins and dancers flood in to join the musical celebration.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_JACKSON_HANDBOOK_STO: Dancing Zombie's latest record, Grab That Brain and Gnaw, Gnaw, Gnaw, is rocketing up the zombie charts.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_JALAPENO_HANDBOOK_ST: Jalapeno Zombie does not know what sits on his head—perhaps a consequence of spicy hotpot with friends. The pressure has become difficult to control. He has waited a long time for the moment when friendship demands release.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_LMITATER_HANDBOOK_ST: A celebrated zombie comedian, Imitater Zombie good-naturedly joins others in calling himself Eggplant Head. “I don't wash? Please—an Imitater is supposed to look dusty and gray!”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_MAGNETIC_HANDBOOK_ST: He is magnetic, but never fickle. Zombies love Magnetic Field Zombie drawing fire for them; only Screen Door Zombie complains that he ruins their pea-ping-pong games.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_MELONPULT_HANDBOOK_S: Melon-pult Zombie loved eating melons and littering. His current head delights him because it satisfies both habits at once.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_MERCHANT_HANDBOOK_ST: Market Zombie claims nobody understands economics better and lectures Tycoon Zombie over wine. Ask how he became undead or why Plantern terrifies him, and he changes the subject.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_NECROMANCERB_HANDBOO: Giant Mage Zombie was once a doctor researching height treatments. “We're already zombies, so I tried everything. In the end, this worked best.” He proudly waves his staff.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_NECROMANCERG_HANDBOO: “No living being escapes death; neither did I,” murmurs Rebirth Mage, raising his staff. “But we have already died once. It is time for a little miracle and magic.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_NECROMANCER_HANDBOOK: Specially trained by Zomboss, this mage has more combat experience than ordinary zombies. Its dark magic creates greater danger—and more mixed waste in the form of broken bones.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_NEWSPAPER_HANDBOOK_S: Newspaper Zombie was one square away from finishing his sudoku. No wonder he became furious.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_NORMAL_HANDBOOK_STOR: This zombie craves brains without limit. Brains, brains, brains—day and night. Smelly brains? Rotten brains? It makes no difference.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_NUT_HANDBOOK_STORY: Wall-nut Zombie loves bowling and found a bowling-ball helmet by the roadside. Nobody told him it was actually a Wall-nut.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_PAPERBALL_HANDBOOK_S: The most intellectual athlete and most athletic intellectual among zombies reads sports news while solving sudoku. Losing the paper sends him into a rage beyond even a kindly “Uncle” calming down.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_PEASHOOTERSINGLE_HAN: Faced with today's terrifying plants, ordinary zombies miss the old Peashooter. One once reached a brain, then instinctively spat it out as though it were a pea.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_PEASHOOTER_HANDBOOK_: The most successful zombie imitation of Repeater is also the quickest to grow hungry. He lives by one rule: a single brain is not worthy of his mouth.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POGOBALL_HANDBOOK_ST: Pogo Ball Zombie unquestionably wants brains most, because his doctor warned him about concussions.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POGODANCER_HANDBOOK_: Chewilliard never taught this style of dance, but every art needs innovation.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POGOJACKSON_HANDBOOK: Perhaps this is what “jump dancing” truly means.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POGO_HANDBOOK_STORY: Boing! Boing! Boing! The strong, efficient sound of Pogo Zombie.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POLESTRIKER_HANDBOOK:
Charging Football Pole Vaulter asked his coach which sport to pursue. “You score only fifty in football and fifty in pole vaulting, so...”
“Wait! I never said combine them!”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POLEVAULTING_HANDBOO: Some zombies yearn to go farther and achieve more, transforming the ordinary into the extraordinary. Pole Vaulting Zombie is one.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_PORTAL_HANDBOOK_STOR: Zomboss's latest invention is a portable portal that returns plant projectiles. He forgot that only plant shots pass through, so they still belong to the plants—and the battery quickly dies.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_POT_HANDBOOK_STORY: To make ends meet, Ladder Zombie sold his beloved ladder. He now works carrying vases.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_PRESENTBOX_HANDBOOK_: Prize Box Zombie does not know what rests above him. The unopened box may release something when broken. Unsure whether he will remain himself afterward, he nonetheless sometimes wishes someone would open it.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SCREEN_DOOR_HANDBOOK: The last homeowner Screen Door Zombie visited had poor defenses. After eating the owner's brain, he took the screen door.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SEADEMON_HANDBOOK_ST: Siren Zombie believes he was once a mighty sea demon and even stole a neighbor's pitchfork. Everyone knows he was merely dragged underwater by Tangle Kelp repeatedly. Worse, he has begun singing lessons.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SHADOW_HANDBOOK_STOR: Every zombie has a shadow, but they envy Shadow Zombie's freely moving, perfectly upright one. “Why? An upright body fears no crooked shadow,” he explains.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SHARK_HANDBOOK_STORY: A giant once used him as a club and gave him a concussion, yet he still plays the shark. Why? Peer pressure, naturally.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SHIELDARMOR_HANDBOOK: Zomboss's laboratory lacks professional safety equipment. To complete his blast protection, Blastproof Door Zombie removed the lab's own blast door before leaving.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SKELETON_HANDBOOK_ST: Enhanced by mysterious Zomboss technology, these self-proclaimed elites say a fleshless body makes them feel light. Whether truly elite is unclear; Chomper merely warns, “Broken bones are sharp. Chew carefully.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SKELETUAR_HANDBOOK_S: Nobody knows why Skeleton Gargantuar is so painfully thin. Perhaps he believes such a bare-bones outfit will help him find a girlfriend.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SLEEP_HANDBOOK_STORY: “Where's my sled? No penguin or motorcycle to help? At least there's still a yeti,” mumbles Tumbler Zombie before returning to sleep, unaware that his bed is about to break.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SNORKLE_DOOMTANGLEKE: Few things are worse than an explosive head, falling into water, and becoming tangled in kelp. Doom Kelp Snorkel Zombie no longer cares. He can swim that hateful head toward hateful plants and—boom—make everything disappear.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SNORKLE_HANDBOOK_STO: Zombies do not breathe, so why does Snorkel Zombie need elaborate diving gear? Peer pressure.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SNORKLE_TANGLEKELP_H: Snorkel Zombie hates Tangle Kelp. He hates what he has become even more.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SNOWPEA_HANDBOOK_STO: Snow Pea Zombie is terrified of modern hybrid plants. Trembling, he cannot help shivering.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SOCCER_HANDBOOK_STOR: Zombie News reports a milestone in the soccer team's league campaign and enormous progress over the football brutes: they finally learned that soccer is played with the feet.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SPECIALHELMET_HANDBO: Zomboss found an old gladiator helmet in storage. “Time to put it to use!” Its wearer charges like a true gladiator—unless Magnet-shroom removes the buckles and rivets.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SQUASH_HANDBOOK_STOR: How many steps does Squash Zombie need to flatten a plant? Two. First, charge any plant. Second: “Huh?!”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_STARFRUIT_HANDBOOK_S: “I'm seeing stars,” says Starfruit Zombie. “It disrupts my life.” As an astronomy enthusiast, he still does not regret standing inside the meteor shower's danger zone.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SUNFLOWER_HANDBOOK_S: “I want to join the Sunflowers, but they call me a sunlight thief. Yet I produce light!” Sunflower Zombie tells a therapist. After consultation with ophthalmology, the diagnosis is final: color blindness.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_SWANRIDER_HANDBOOK_S: Swan Rider plans to name his mount Nils. He may have confused the names in the story.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_TALLNUT_HANDBOOK_STO: Tall-nut Zombie hears others whisper that he looks top-heavy. He feels perfectly balanced—perhaps the head is lighter than it looks, or perhaps it contains no brain.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_TARGET_HANDBOOK_STOR: Target Zombie has held his sign for years, sometimes as an objective to defend and sometimes as firing practice. He merely stands still. Occasionally he longs to set it down and walk, if only to remember that he is a zombie rather than a target stand.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_THREEPEATER_HANDBOOK: “Three heads mean a head survives every hit!” Threepeater Zombie once boasted. He regretted it when school charged triple tuition and work paid only one salary.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_UFO_HANDBOOK_STORY: A survey craft from the PC2009 galaxy, whose zombie species arose thirty minutes after the local humans. Zomboss appears to have arranged some form of cooperation.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_VAMPIRE_HANDBOOK_STO: Vampire Zombie promotes a green diet, claiming vegetarianism cured his ultraviolet allergy. Unfortunately, he remains severely allergic to garlic.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_WALLNUTABC_HANDBOOK_: The thickest skin in the zombie world.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_WILDPEA_HANDBOOK_STO: Wild is the nickname Gatling Zombie treasures most. “See my head? It will teach you the true meaning of crazy!”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_WINTERMELONPULT_HAND: Winter Melon Zombie is the busiest plant-zombie, dodging both plants and hungry children. When he stops as if resting or thinking, he is actually frozen stiff.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_YETIDIGGER_HANDBOOK_: He mined snowy mountains until his hair turned gray. After losing one boot in a desert gold mine, he has now lost both. Digger Zombie had to lend him another pair.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_YETIFOOTBALL_HANDBOO: Facing a roster shortage, the football coach found this athletic recruit deep in the mountains. Two details escaped him: Yeti cannot bear the uniform's heat and knows nothing about football.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ZAMBONIPULT_HANDBOOK: When his shaved-ice stand struggled, he tried selling from a moving vehicle. His sales technique may be excessively enthusiastic.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ZOMBONI_GATLINGPEA_H: Gatling Zombie retakes his Zomboni license every year after repeated dangerous driving and uncontrollable pea fire. “I get motion sickness, but driving looks too cool.”
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ZOMBONI_HANDBOOK_STO: Often mistaken for zombies driving ice machines, Zombonis are reportedly a distinct life-form more closely related to space orks.
TOWERDEFENSE_ZOMBIE_ZOMBONI_ICESHROOM_HA: Ice-shroom Zombie's Zomboni is really a refrigerator, and he sleeps inside every night. Each freezing blast is not his power—the refrigerator simply exploded.
